3.7 Data Governance and Compliance:
To ensure that the proposed solution meets stringent standards for data governance and compliance, our approach integrates comprehensive mechanisms across security, master data management, metadata stewardship, and regulatory adherence.

We will institute robust security controls, anchored in role-based access control (RBAC), granting users access only to the minimum data necessary for their functions. This principle of least privilege will be rigorously enforced across all user profiles—including administrators, analysts, and third-party partners—by integrating with existing identity management systems and supporting single sign-on (SSO) for ease of auditability and user lifecycle management. All access events will be meticulously logged and regularly reviewed to detect and respond to unauthorized access attempts in real time.

To improve data consistency and quality, we will implement an enterprise-class Master Data Management (MDM) framework. This will centralize critical entity domains—such as customer, supplier, and product data—across the organization, providing a single point of truth. Automated data validation, deduplication, and enrichment processes will ensure data integrity, while clearly governed workflows will manage stewardship, approval, and versioning of master data. These capabilities will directly reduce regulatory risk by ensuring the traceability and correctness of reference data used throughout business processes.

Metadata management will be facilitated through the deployment of a modern Data Catalog, providing an intuitive interface for users to discover, classify, and understand available data assets. This system will capture both technical and business metadata, supporting lineage tracing, impact analysis, and stewardship accountability. The Data Catalog will be tightly integrated with data lifecycle management policies, ensuring that the origins, usage, and ownership of all data elements are transparently documented—critical for both operational efficiency and regulatory compliance.

Compliance with local and international data security and privacy frameworks will be embedded into all layers of the solution. Our compliance design will address GDPR for European operations, CCPA for California-based activities, and any applicable local regulations. This includes enforcing data residency requirements, implementing data minimization policies, supporting data subject rights (such as access, rectification, and erasure), and maintaining up-to-date records of processing activities. Encryption protocols—both in transit and at rest—will be standardized according to the highest industry benchmarks (e.g., AES-256), and routine privacy impact assessments will be conducted to monitor adherence and mitigate emerging risks.

Through this layered approach, the solution delivers not only operational efficiency but also a trusted environment where security, stewardship, and regulatory alignment are foundational, supporting the organization's strategic objectives and public trust.

1. Introduction:
Sidra Medicine stands at a critical juncture in its pursuit to become a leading academic medical center, renowned for excellence in care, learning, and discovery. A cornerstone of this vision is Sidra’s commitment to being a fully digital hospital—one that leverages information, data, and insights to drive superior clinical outcomes, groundbreaking research, and seamless operational efficiency.

Currently, Sidra Medicine relies on a robust ecosystem of digital platforms—including Cerner EMR, Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, Datix, Qualtrics, and a suite of specialized research systems—that support every facet of care delivery and hospital administration. These platforms generate vast quantities of data each day, ranging from patient medical records and financial transactions, to quality events, survey feedback, genomic sequencing, biorepository samples, and research registries.

However, the transformative potential of this data remains largely untapped due to its fragmented and siloed storage across disparate applications. Clinicians, researchers, and executives face challenges when attempting to extract, consolidate, and analyze information critical for timely decision-making. Manual processes—such as data extraction and report distribution—consume significant resources and hinder Sidra’s ability to respond rapidly to emerging trends, operational needs, and research opportunities.

To bridge this gap, Sidra Medicine seeks to establish a unified Data Lake and advanced analytics solution, forming a single, trusted repository for all institutional data assets. This ambitious initiative aims not only to eliminate inefficiencies caused by manual data handling, but to unleash the hospital’s full potential as a data-driven institution. By consolidating clinical, administrative, financial, operational, and research data into a secure and accessible platform, Sidra will empower all stakeholders—physicians, scientists, management, and support staff—with timely, actionable insights.

The Data Lake will serve as the foundation for advanced analytics, predictive modeling, and real-time dashboards, enabling Sidra Medicine to uncover hidden trends, optimize resource allocation, and proactively improve the quality and safety of patient care. Moreover, researchers will gain unprecedented access to integrated datasets, accelerating discoveries in genomics, precision medicine, and translational research.

Through this initiative, Sidra Medicine will not only streamline its daily operations, but also position itself at the forefront of healthcare innovation—delivering informed, personalized, and exceptional care to every patient, and setting new standards for academic medical centers worldwide.

3.2 Data Lake / Lakehouse Architecture D:
**3.2 Data Lake / Lakehouse Architecture Design**

To deliver a flexible, scalable, and secure analytics platform, we propose an Azure-based Data Lake/Lakehouse architecture designed around best practices in modern data engineering. This approach will support high-throughput data ingestion, advanced analytics, and comprehensive data governance—all underpinned by the robust toolset available through Microsoft Azure.

**Multi-Zone Data Lake Architecture**

Our architecture separates the data lake into three distinct zones, each optimized for particular data lifecycle stages:

1. **Raw Data Zone**  
   The Raw Data Zone acts as the initial landing area within Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS). Utilizing Azure Data Factory pipelines, raw, source-system data is ingested into dedicated containers, supporting both structured and unstructured formats (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro, images, etc.). Metadata is captured at ingestion using Azure Purview for downstream governance and lineage tracking. This immutable repository ensures full traceability of all ingested data, supporting future data reprocessing and audit requirements.

2. **Cleansed Data Zone**  
   After ingestion, data is processed and transformed within Azure Databricks, leveraging Apache Spark for high-performance cleaning, enrichment, and standardization tasks (e.g., schema enforcement, deduplication, type validation). The cleansed outputs are written back to ADLS in a standardized format (Delta Lake), facilitating high concurrency and ACID transactions. Permissions and data masking policies established via Azure Purview protect sensitive data while supporting compliance requirements.

3. **Curated Data Zone**  
   The Curated Data Zone organizes and presents data tailored to high-value analytical use cases. Here, domain-specific data models are implemented, often denormalized or aggregated for optimal BI and reporting performance. Data is serialized in efficient formats (Delta/Parquet) to support consumption patterns for machine learning, advanced analytics, and real-time dashboards. Data lifecycle policies—driven via Azure Purview—manage data retention, access control, and change tracking, providing a strong governance foundation.

**Subject Area Data Marts**

To optimize analytical performance and facilitate self-service reporting, we provision Azure Synapse Analytics data marts corresponding to key subject areas (e.g., Sales, Supply Chain, Customer, Finance). Data flows from the Curated Data Zone into Synapse dedicated SQL pools where star or snowflake schemas are implemented based on business requirements. Azure Data Factory orchestrates regular ELT workloads, ensuring near real-time data freshness while optimizing compute utilization.

Power BI and other data consumers connect directly to these marts to enable advanced visualization, ad hoc analysis, and exploratory queries with minimal latency. Security roles and row-level security are enforced to ensure granular access control.

**Core Azure Services and Integration**

- **Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS):** Serves as the unified storage layer for all zones, providing scalability, robust security (RBAC, ACLs), and seamless integration with Azure analytics services.
- **Azure Databricks:** Delivers scalable ETL, data science, and streaming workloads, leveraging Delta Lake’s reliability and performance features.
- **Azure Synapse Analytics:** Provides enterprise-grade data warehousing for subject-specific marts, supporting complex SQL queries and integration with linked services.
- **Azure Data Factory:** Powers end-to-end data pipeline orchestration, from ingestion to transformation and loading, with native connectivity to diverse on-premises and cloud sources.
- **Azure Purview:** Establishes comprehensive data governance, cataloging all datasets, tracking lineage, scanning for sensitive information, and enforcing data compliance policies.

**Deliverable: Data Architecture Design Document**

As part of this engagement, we will deliver a detailed Data Architecture Design document, including:

- End-to-end logical and physical architecture diagrams
- Data flow and lifecycle mapping for all zones
- Design specifications for subject area data marts (schemas, refresh strategy, SLAs)
- Integration details across ADLS, Databricks, Synapse, Data Factory, and Purview
- Data security, privacy, and governance controls
- Recommendations for scalability, monitoring, and future extensibility

This solution ensures your data platform is ready for advanced analytics, delivering business value while maintaining the highest standards of quality, governance, and performance.

3.4 Data Ingestion and Integration:
To meet the diverse requirements of data ingestion and integration, our proposed solution delivers robust, scalable, and high-performance pipelines tailored to efficiently handle both batch and real-time data scenarios.

**Batch Data Ingestion:**  
Leveraging Azure Data Factory (ADF), we will orchestrate end-to-end data pipelines capable of ingesting large volumes of data from various distributed sources—on-premises databases, cloud storage, SaaS platforms, and external APIs. ADF’s native connectivity and monitoring capabilities provide a resilient foundation, ensuring data is reliably acquired, error-handled, and auditable with comprehensive logging metrics. Pipelines will be optimized for incremental loads, reducing unnecessary data movement and enabling timely refreshes for downstream analytics.

**Real-Time Data Ingestion:**  
For scenarios demanding immediate data processing, we will implement real-time ingestion utilizing Azure Event Hubs and Azure Stream Analytics. Event Hubs will capture high-throughput event streams (such as IoT telemetry, application logs, or transactional feeds) from multiple producers, preserving ordering and enabling scale-out consumers. Downstream, Azure Stream Analytics will process, analyze, and filter these incoming events in real time, allowing for actionable insights with millisecond latency. The processed data will seamlessly integrate into data lakes, warehouses, or operational dashboards.

**Data Integration, Processing, and Transformation:**  
All ingested data will be unified through robust ETL/ELT pipelines. Using Data Factory and native Azure Data Services, we will design modular, reusable workflows that integrate disparate datasets, perform thorough data cleansing (e.g., deduplication, standardization, validation), and execute complex transformations to prepare the data for advanced analytics. Business rules and transformation logic will be implemented using a combination of Data Flow activities and Spark-based transformations for scalability.

To maximize performance and cost-efficiency, pipelines will be designed to leverage ELT patterns where feasible—loading raw data quickly into a centralized data store (e.g., Azure Synapse, Data Lake Storage) and performing in-place transformations using optimized compute resources. This decouples ingestion speed from transformation complexity and allows stakeholders to access raw or processed data according to their needs.

3.6 Data Storage and Management:
To ensure robust, scalable, and high-performance data storage and management, our solution leverages Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS) for flexible raw and processed data organization, and Azure Synapse Analytics for optimized structured storage supporting analytics and reporting needs.

Within Azure Data Lake Storage, we will implement a multi-layer folder structure, separating raw (landing zone), cleansed (curated zone), and enriched (gold zone) datasets. Data will be organized hierarchically by business domain, source system, ingestion date, and data sensitivity, allowing for secure access controls, efficient data lifecycle management, and streamlined ETL processes. Metadata management will be integrated using Azure Purview, ensuring all assets are catalogued and governed for discovery and compliance.

For Azure Synapse Analytics, we will employ a deliberate approach to table design, indexing, and partitioning to meet both performance and cost objectives. Tables will be modelled using dedicated SQL pools for large-scale, persistent data, with ClearStar schema design principles to minimize data redundancy and enhance query performance. Fact tables will be partitioned on key dimensions such as date or geography, dramatically reducing query scan times and enabling incremental data loads. Clustered columnstore indexing will be applied to large fact tables to maximize compression and analytic query performance, while clustered/nonclustered indexes will support high selectivity lookup scenarios on dimension tables.

Together, these strategies provide a unified, governed, and high-throughput data platform. Fine-grained access policies and data retention rules will be applied to both ADLS and Synapse artifacts, ensuring security and regulatory compliance. By combining hierarchical storage in ADLS and optimized analytical structures within Synapse, we enable seamless, end-to-end data management—supporting current analytical needs and laying the foundation for future data science, AI, and business intelligence initiatives.
